Standard deviation of binary data

Source: R/sd-binary.R
sd-binary.Rd

Compute the SD of binary data (0 and 1 values) from different inputs:

  • sd_binary_groups() from the counts of 0s and 1s.

  • sd_binary_0_n() from the count of 0s and the total.

  • sd_binary_1_n() from the count of 1s and the total.

  • sd_binary_mean_n() from the mean and the total.

These are the SDs that debit() tests under the same sd_meaning.

sd_binary_0_n() and sd_binary_1_n() are superseded by sd_binary_groups(): sd_binary_0_n(group_0, n) is sd_binary_groups(group_0, n - group_0).

Usage

sd_binary_groups(
  group_0,
  group_1,
  sd_meaning = c("sd_sample", "sd_pop", "sd_sample_or_pop", "se")
)

sd_binary_0_n(
  group_0,
  n,
  sd_meaning = c("sd_sample", "sd_pop", "sd_sample_or_pop", "se")
)

sd_binary_1_n(
  group_1,
  n,
  sd_meaning = c("sd_sample", "sd_pop", "sd_sample_or_pop", "se")
)

sd_binary_mean_n(
  x,
  n,
  sd_meaning = c("sd_sample", "sd_pop", "sd_sample_or_pop", "se"),
  mean = deprecated()
)

Arguments

group_0

Integer. Count of 0s.

group_1

Integer. Count of 1s.

sd_meaning

String. What to compute: the sample SD, "sd_sample" (the default); the population SD, "sd_pop"; or the standard error of the mean, "se", as in debit(). "sd_sample_or_pop" is an error here, since it stands for two premises with different values.

n

Integer. Total sample size.

x

Numeric. Mean of the data, i.e., the share of 1s.

mean

The old name of x.

Value

Numeric. The SD or standard error; NA where n or a count is not a whole number, and where n is below 2 under "sd_sample" and "se", which divide by n - 1.

References

Heathers, James A. J., and Brown, Nicholas J. L. 2019. DEBIT: A Simple Consistency Test For Binary Data. https://osf.io/5vb3u/.

Examples

# 127 values are 0 and 153 are 1, so n = 280:
sd_binary_groups(group_0 = 127, group_1 = 153)
#> [1] 0.4987311
sd_binary_0_n(group_0 = 127, n = 280)
#> [1] 0.4987311
sd_binary_1_n(group_1 = 153, n = 280)
#> [1] 0.4987311

# From the mean, given enough decimal places:
sd_binary_mean_n(x = 0.5464286, n = 280)
#> [1] 0.4987311

# The population SD and the standard error:
sd_binary_groups(group_0 = 127, group_1 = 153, sd_meaning = "sd_pop")
#> [1] 0.4978397
sd_binary_groups(group_0 = 127, group_1 = 153, sd_meaning = "se")
#> [1] 0.02980488
